What makes Canopy different

Designed to live in,
not just to look at

Canopy is not a street. It is a thoughtfully master-planned neighbourhood within Glendalough, developed by Stockland and designed by Urbis. The magnificent Fig Tree at the heart of the community gives the estate its name and character. Streets are designed as communal living spaces, with traffic calming, footpaths, cycleways, and homes that engage with the street. Walkability and community are central to the design, so you can leave the car at home and get to know your neighbours.

Direct sale, no agent

How to buy
directly from the owner

Buying direct is straightforward. No agent manages the process, no communication filter sits between you and the decision-maker, and no commission stake inflates the negotiation. Here is how it works.

1
Inspect the property
Attend an open home or request a private inspection. Walk through at your own pace. Ask us anything directly. We know this home better than any agent could.
2
Get your finance in order
Speak to your bank or mortgage broker. Know your borrowing capacity and have pre-approval in place before making a formal offer. This puts you in the strongest negotiating position.
3
Engage a settlement agent or conveyancer
You will need a licensed WA settlement agent or solicitor to prepare and handle the offer and contract documentation. This is standard practice for all property transactions in Western Australia. Search the Australian Institute of Conveyancers WA Division at aicwa.com.au.
4
Submit your offer in writing
Your settlement agent will prepare a standard REIWA offer and acceptance contract. Email it to us directly. We will review and respond promptly. No gatekeeper, no delay.
5
Negotiate directly with us
If we need to discuss price or conditions, that conversation happens between us, owner to buyer. No messages passed through a third party. No commission stake in the outcome shaping the result. A straightforward negotiation.
A typical agent commission in WA is 2 to 3 per cent of the sale price. On a $1.4 million transaction that is $28,000 to $42,000. In a direct sale, that cost does not exist on either side. We price this home at what it is worth, and both parties benefit from the simpler structure.
